meta.title: The Braided Crowns of Europe
meta.subtitle: Major European monarchies from the Roman Principate to the present
meta.scope_note: The overview includes historically consequential sovereign monarchies, predecessor realms needed to explain later states, and every surviving European monarchy. Tier 2 contains regionally important or shorter-lived realms. Dates are editorial periodizations and are documented in source notes.

sources.title: Kingdom of Sicily and the Two Sicilies
Dissolution of European empires after World War I

polities.name: Roman Empire
polities.summary: The Roman imperial state from Augustus to the permanent administrative division of 395.

polities.name: Western Roman Empire
polities.summary: The western imperial court after the division of 395, ending conventionally in 476.

polities.name: Eastern Roman / Byzantine Empire
polities.summary: The eastern Roman imperial state centred on Constantinople; modern scholarship conventionally calls its medieval phase Byzantine.

polities.name: Frankish Realm (Francia)
polities.summary: Francia is the historical name used here for the Merovingian and Carolingian Frankish realm. It ends with the 843 partition that created West, Middle and East Francia.

polities.name: Holy Roman Empire
polities.summary: A composite elective empire in Central Europe. This project begins the continuous imperial phase with Otto I in 962 and treats Charlemagne's coronation as a precursor event.

polities.name: French Monarchy
polities.summary: This lane begins with West Francia after the partition of the wider Frankish realm in 843, then follows the Kingdom of France and the Bourbon and July restorations.

polities.name: Kingdom of England
polities.summary: The unified English kingdom until the Acts of Union created Great Britain in 1707.

polities.name: Kingdom of Scotland
polities.summary: The Scottish kingdom until the parliamentary union with England in 1707.

polities.name: Kingdom of Great Britain
polities.summary: The state created by the union of England and Scotland, lasting until union with Ireland in 1801.

polities.name: United Kingdom
polities.summary: The constitutional monarchy created in 1801 and continued after most of Ireland left the union.

polities.name: Crown of Castile
polities.summary: The composite Crown of Castile, joined dynastically with Aragon and later integrated into the Spanish monarchy.

polities.name: Crown of Aragon
polities.summary: A composite Mediterranean monarchy joined dynastically with Castile in the late fifteenth century.

polities.name: Kingdom of Navarre
polities.summary: A Pyrenean kingdom divided between Spain and France; the northern kingdom was incorporated into France in 1620.

polities.name: Kingdom of Portugal
polities.summary: The Portuguese monarchy from its twelfth-century independence to the republic of 1910.

polities.name: Spain
polities.summary: The Spanish monarchy, shown first as the dynastic union of Castile and Aragon, then as a more centralized state, with twentieth-century interruptions.

polities.name: Denmark
polities.summary: One of Europe's oldest continuing monarchies, central to the Kalmar Union and Denmark–Norway.

polities.name: Norway
polities.summary: The Norwegian monarchy, including long periods of personal union with Denmark and Sweden.

polities.name: Sweden
polities.summary: The Swedish monarchy from medieval consolidation through the Vasa empire and Bernadotte dynasty.

polities.name: Kingdom of Poland
polities.summary: The Polish kingdom, later joined first personally and then constitutionally with Lithuania.

polities.name: Grand Duchy of Lithuania
polities.summary: A major eastern European grand duchy joined with Poland under the Jagiellons and the Union of Lublin.

polities.name: Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth
polities.summary: A federative elective monarchy created by the Union of Lublin and ended by the partitions of Poland.

polities.name: Kingdom of Bohemia
polities.summary: A kingdom of the Bohemian Crown within the Holy Roman Empire and later the Habsburg monarchy.

polities.name: Kingdom of Hungary
polities.summary: The Hungarian crown from Stephen I through Habsburg rule; the regency of 1920–1946 retained the name kingdom without a king.

polities.name: Archduchy and Empire of Austria
polities.summary: The Habsburg hereditary lands and Austrian Empire before the dual monarchy of 1867.

polities.name: Austria-Hungary
polities.summary: The Dual Monarchy created by the Austro-Hungarian Compromise and dissolved in 1918.

polities.name: Tsardom and Empire of Russia
polities.summary: The Russian monarchy from Ivan IV's coronation as tsar to the revolutions of 1917.

polities.name: Kingdom of Prussia
polities.summary: The Hohenzollern kingdom that led German unification and became the largest constituent state of the German Empire.

polities.name: German Empire
polities.summary: The federal German monarchy proclaimed in 1871 under the Prussian Hohenzollerns.

polities.name: Kingdom of the Netherlands
polities.summary: The constitutional monarchy created after the Napoleonic Wars under Orange-Nassau.

polities.name: Belgium
polities.summary: The constitutional monarchy established after the Belgian Revolution.

polities.name: Savoy and the Kingdom of Sardinia
polities.summary: The Savoyard monarchy that became the Kingdom of Sardinia and led Italian unification.

polities.name: Kingdom of Italy
polities.summary: The Savoy monarchy of united Italy, ended by referendum after the Second World War.

polities.name: Sicily and the Two Sicilies
polities.summary: The southern Italian monarchy created by the Normans and reunited as the Two Sicilies in 1816.

polities.name: Serbian Kingdoms
polities.summary: The medieval Serbian kingdom and empire, followed by the modern kingdom that helped form Yugoslavia.

polities.name: Kingdom of Yugoslavia
polities.summary: The South Slav monarchy formed in 1918 and abolished after the Second World War.

polities.name: Bulgarian Empires and Kingdom
polities.summary: The medieval Bulgarian empires and the modern kingdom abolished in 1946.

polities.name: Kingdom of Romania
polities.summary: The Romanian monarchy under Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen, ended in 1947.

polities.name: Kingdom of Greece
polities.summary: The modern Greek monarchy, interrupted in 1924 and finally abolished in 1973–1974.

polities.name: Ottoman Empire
polities.summary: A transcontinental sultanate included because its European territories and diplomacy were central to European monarchical history.

polities.name: Kingdom of Croatia
polities.summary: The medieval Croatian kingdom before its personal union with Hungary.

polities.name: Grand Duchy of Luxembourg
polities.summary: The world's only surviving sovereign grand duchy.

polities.name: Principality of Monaco
polities.summary: The Grimaldi principality, included among Europe's surviving hereditary monarchies.

polities.name: Principality of Liechtenstein
polities.summary: A surviving Alpine principality ruled by the House of Liechtenstein.

polities.name: Co-Principality of Andorra
polities.summary: A parliamentary co-principality whose joint heads are the Bishop of Urgell and the French head of state.

polities.name: Papal States and Vatican City
polities.summary: The temporal papal monarchy, interrupted after 1870 and restored in Vatican City in 1929.

phases.name: Unified Roman imperial state
phases.note: The start date follows Augustus' constitutional settlement of 27 BCE; the state itself did not call this a new kingdom.

phases.name: Eastern Roman Empire
phases.note: The label Byzantine is a modern historiographical convention.

phases.name: Frankish Kingdom and Carolingian Empire
phases.note: This broader Frankish realm is labelled Francia to distinguish it from the France lane that begins with West Francia after the Treaty of Verdun.

phases.name: Continuous imperial phase
phases.note: Charlemagne's imperial coronation in 800 is shown as a precursor event rather than the continuous start of this lane.

phases.name: West Francia and Kingdom of France
Crown of Aragon
phases.note: The project uses 1035 for the kingdom's independent dynastic start and 1715 for integration under the Nueva Planta settlement.

phases.name: Dynastic monarchy of Spain
phases.note: Castile and Aragon retained separate institutions; the shared lane marks a dynastic monarchy, not a fully unified state.

phases.name: Kingdom without a king
phases.note: Miklós Horthy governed as regent; the lane is marked distinctly because no monarch occupied the throne.

phases.name: Kingdom of Sicily and successor crowns
Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes / Yugoslavia

relationships.label: Administrative division of the Roman Empire
relationships.description: After Theodosius I, separate imperial courts governed the western and eastern halves. The division became permanent even though both remained Roman in identity.

relationships.label: End of the western imperial court
relationships.description: The deposition of Romulus Augustulus conventionally marks the end of the Western Roman Empire, though Roman institutions and successor kingdoms continued.

relationships.label: Roman continuity in the east
relationships.description: The eastern empire understood itself as the Roman Empire; Byzantine is a later scholarly label.

relationships.label: Treaty of Verdun
relationships.description: The Carolingian realm was divided among Louis the Pious's sons. West Francia developed into France; the eastern realm belongs to the precursor story of the Holy Roman Empire.

relationships.label: Fall of Constantinople
relationships.description: Mehmed II captured Constantinople, ending the Eastern Roman imperial state.

relationships.label: Union of the Crowns
relationships.description: James VI of Scotland inherited the English and Irish crowns as James I while the kingdoms retained separate institutions.

relationships.label: Acts of Union
relationships.description: The English and Scottish parliaments united their kingdoms into Great Britain.

relationships.label: Union with Ireland
relationships.description: Great Britain and Ireland formed the United Kingdom in 1801; the state's name changed after most of Ireland left in the twentieth century.

relationships.label: Dynastic union of Castile and Aragon
relationships.description: The marriage and joint rule of Isabella of Castile and Ferdinand of Aragon created a shared monarchy while the crowns kept distinct laws and institutions.

relationships.label: Nueva Planta settlement
relationships.description: The Nueva Planta decrees reorganized the Spanish monarchy and suppressed many separate institutions of the Crown of Aragon.

relationships.label: Iberian Union
relationships.description: The Spanish Habsburgs ruled Portugal in personal union until the Portuguese Restoration.

relationships.label: Portuguese Restoration
relationships.description: The Braganza revolt restored an independent Portuguese monarch.

relationships.label: Kalmar Union
relationships.description: Denmark, Norway and Sweden shared a monarch under the Kalmar Union while remaining distinct kingdoms.

relationships.label: Denmark–Norway
relationships.description: The Danish monarch ruled Norway in a composite state until the Napoleonic settlement of 1814.

relationships.label: Sweden–Norway
relationships.description: Norway retained its constitution and institutions while sharing a monarch with Sweden.

relationships.label: Polish–Lithuanian dynastic union
relationships.description: The marriage of Jadwiga and Jogaila established a long personal and dynastic union.

relationships.label: Union of Lublin
relationships.description: The Union of Lublin created a federative Commonwealth with an elected joint monarch.

relationships.label: Partitions of the Commonwealth
relationships.description: The third partition ended the Commonwealth and divided its remaining territory among Russia, Prussia and Austria.

relationships.label: Dissolution of the Holy Roman Empire
relationships.description: Francis II abdicated the imperial crown during the Napoleonic reorganization of Germany. Austria and Prussia became the leading German monarchies but were not direct constitutional successors.

relationships.label: Austro-Hungarian Compromise
relationships.description: The Habsburg monarchy became a dual state with Austrian and Hungarian governments under one sovereign.

relationships.label: German unification
relationships.description: The Prussian king became German emperor in a federal monarchy dominated by Prussia.

relationships.label: Italian unification
relationships.description: The Savoyard Kingdom of Sardinia became the Kingdom of Italy after incorporating most Italian states, including the Two Sicilies.

relationships.label: South Slav kingdom
relationships.description: The Serbian crown became the monarchy of the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes, renamed Yugoslavia in 1929.

relationships.label: Byzantine conquest of Bulgaria
relationships.description: Basil II completed the conquest of the First Bulgarian Empire.

relationships.label: Second Bulgarian Empire
relationships.description: The Asen uprising restored an independent Bulgarian monarchy.

relationships.label: Ottoman conquest of Bulgaria
relationships.description: Ottoman conquest ended the medieval Bulgarian imperial state.

relationships.label: Ottoman conquest of Serbia
relationships.description: The fall of Smederevo ended the medieval Serbian Despotate.

relationships.label: Bourbon Restoration
relationships.description: The Bourbon monarchy returned after Napoleon's defeat, with a brief interruption during the Hundred Days.

relationships.label: Restoration of the Spanish monarchy
relationships.description: Juan Carlos I became king after Francisco Franco's death and presided over the transition to constitutional democracy.

relationships.label: Restoration of the Greek monarchy
relationships.description: A controlled plebiscite restored George II after the Second Hellenic Republic.

relationships.label: Lateran Treaty
relationships.description: The Lateran Treaty created Vatican City and restored temporal sovereignty to the pope after the loss of the Papal States.

relationships.label: Russian Revolution
relationships.description: Nicholas II abdicated during the February Revolution, ending the Romanov monarchy.

relationships.label: End of the Central European empires
relationships.description: Defeat and revolution ended the German and Austro-Hungarian monarchies.

relationships.label: Abolition of the Ottoman sultanate
relationships.description: The Turkish Grand National Assembly abolished the sultanate.

relationships.label: Italian republic
relationships.description: A referendum ended the Savoy monarchy and established the Italian Republic.

relationships.label: End of the Balkan monarchies
relationships.description: Communist governments abolished the Yugoslav, Bulgarian and Romanian monarchies after the Second World War.

events.label: Augustan settlement
events.description: Octavian received the title Augustus, conventionally beginning the Roman Principate.

events.label: Permanent imperial division
events.description: Separate western and eastern courts followed the death of Theodosius I.

events.label: Western emperor deposed
events.description: Odoacer deposed Romulus Augustulus.

events.label: Charlemagne crowned emperor
events.description: Pope Leo III crowned Charlemagne in Rome, reviving an imperial title in western Europe.

events.label: Treaty of Verdun
events.description: The Carolingian realm was divided into western, middle and eastern kingdoms.

events.label: Otto I crowned emperor
events.description: Otto I's coronation begins the continuous imperial line used for the Holy Roman Empire lane.

events.label: Norman Conquest
events.description: William of Normandy conquered England and replaced the ruling house.

events.label: Fourth Crusade sacks Constantinople
events.description: Crusaders captured Constantinople; Byzantine successor states restored the empire in 1261.

events.label: Fall of Constantinople
events.description: The Ottoman capture ended the Eastern Roman Empire.

events.label: Castile and Aragon share monarchs
events.description: Ferdinand succeeded in Aragon while Isabella already ruled Castile.

events.label: Charles V elected emperor
events.description: The Habsburg ruler of Spain gained the imperial crown.

events.label: Union of Lublin
events.description: Poland and Lithuania formed the Commonwealth.

events.label: Union of the Crowns
events.description: James VI of Scotland inherited England as James I.

events.label: Peace of Westphalia
events.description: The treaties reshaped sovereignty within the Holy Roman Empire and concluded the Thirty Years' War.

events.label: Acts of Union
events.description: England and Scotland became Great Britain.

events.label: Nueva Planta settlement
events.description: The Bourbon monarchy centralized many institutions of Spain.

events.label: French monarchy abolished
events.description: The National Convention proclaimed the French Republic.

events.label: Holy Roman Empire dissolved
events.description: Francis II laid down the imperial crown during the Napoleonic Wars.

events.label: Congress of Vienna settlement
events.description: The post-Napoleonic settlement restored and created monarchies across Europe.

events.label: Revolutions of 1848
events.description: Revolutions challenged monarchies across France, the German states, Italy and the Habsburg lands.

events.label: Kingdom of Italy proclaimed
events.description: Victor Emmanuel II became king of a newly united Italy.

events.label: German Empire proclaimed
events.description: William I of Prussia became German emperor.

events.label: Russian monarchy falls
events.description: Nicholas II abdicated amid revolution.

events.label: Four imperial monarchies collapse
events.description: War and revolution ended the German, Austro-Hungarian and Russian monarchies; the Ottoman sultanate followed in 1922.

events.label: Postwar monarchies abolished
events.description: Referendums and communist takeovers ended several European monarchies after the Second World War.

events.label: Spanish monarchy restored
events.description: Juan Carlos I succeeded Franco as head of state.

events.label: Frederik X succeeds Margrethe II
events.description: Margrethe II abdicated and Frederik X became king of Denmark.

events.label: Transitions in Luxembourg, Andorra and Vatican City
events.description: Guillaume became Grand Duke of Luxembourg, Josep-Lluís Serrano Pentinat became Episcopal Co-Prince of Andorra, and Leo XIV became pope and sovereign of Vatican City.

presets.title: The Carolingian partition
presets.description: The Treaty of Verdun divided the Carolingian Empire and established political lines that shaped France, Germany and the middle kingdom.

presets.title: A conqueror in England
presets.description: The Norman Conquest changed the English ruling house and tied the kingdom more tightly to continental politics.

presets.title: The crowns of Charles V
presets.description: Charles V's election as emperor joined Habsburg possessions across Iberia, Central Europe, Italy and the Low Countries under one monarch.

presets.title: A kingdom of Great Britain
presets.description: A century after the Union of the Crowns, England and Scotland became one state while Iberian and Nordic composite monarchies were also changing.

presets.title: Europe after Napoleon
presets.description: The Congress of Vienna restored and rearranged monarchies while recognizing new kingdoms and dynastic settlements.

presets.title: The fall of four empires
presets.description: War and revolution ended the German, Austro-Hungarian, Russian and Ottoman imperial monarchies and remade the map of Europe.

presets.label: Today
presets.title: Europe's surviving monarchies
presets.description: Twelve sovereign European states retain monarchical heads of state, ranging from kingdoms to a grand duchy, principalities and an elective papacy.
